Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

concubine noun

also kept woman, mistress (a lover), live-in lover, the other woman, paramour

classical

Plaut. Epid. 466: mihi concubīna quae sit
Cic. de Or. 1.183 (Lewis & Short)

concubīna, concubīnae f.

noun, first declension

a woman who lives with a man without being his wife

A less reproachful word than paelex (Lewis & Short). A man kept in the same way is concubīnus.

Other words

  • paelex (pēlex), paelicis f. — the mistress of a married man, as his wife sees her; a rival

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Merc. 690: tuam Alcumēnam paelicem, Jūnō mea; Cic. Clu. 199: fīliae paelex (Lewis & Short)

    With the genitive of the wife she wrongs. The jurist Masurius, in the Digest: the old paelex is now called amīca, or more politely concubīna (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • ego illam volō hodiē facere lībertam meam, mihi concubīna quae sit

    I mean to make her my freedwoman today, to be my concubinePlaut. Epid. 465–466

  • Ei hāc mēcum, ut videās semul tuam Alcumēnam paelicem, Jūnō mea.

    Come this way with me, my Juno, and see your rival, your Alcmena, as well.Plaut. Merc. 689b–690

See also lover, prostitute, mistress, adulterer, wife.

SourcesLewis & Short: concubinus · Lewis & Short: paelex

Plautus, Epidicus 465–466; Mercator 689b–690.
